text:
maria: FYI I landed the kernel-picker fallback last night — quick bench shows a regression on Mistral/Mixtral when rope_scale != 1.0 and using GQA paths. 12% throughput drop on dev machines.
aj: ugh. repro steps? config?
maria: nightly bench on dev1, model=mistral-7b, num_kv_heads=32, kv_dim=64, batch=8, rope_scale=1.2 vs 1.0. 1.0 is fine, 1.2 regresses when the GQA branch is chosen.
benchbot: automated summary attached:
```
config           | throughput tok/s | p50 ms | p99 ms
rope_scale=1.0   | 1280             | 31     | 120
rope_scale=1.2   | 1110             | 38     | 190
delta            | -13.3%           | +22%   | +58%
```
devon: profiler points at extra memcpy in kv-page path when kernel fallback is triggered. looks like we flip from packed-kernel (fast matmul) to generic path that insists on copying into contiguous KV buffer. fragmentation count spikes.
maria: snippet from runtime log where picker chooses kernel:
```
[2023-11-12 03:21:07] selected_kernel: packed_fused_gqa (heads=32, kv_dim=64)
[2023-11-12 03:21:07] fallback_reason: rope_scale_mismatch -> fall back to generic_fp16
[2023-11-12 03:21:07] kv_copy_bytes: +12MB
```
aj: why rope_scale_mismatch? I thought kernels should be invariant to rope scaling value, only to dims/heads.
devon: current kernel eligibility check inspects rope_phase table normalization and rejects packed path if observed phase != table_base for perf-safety. but rope_scale slightly changes interpolation causing the check to fail for some sequences.
sam: I tried a quick change to relax the check (tolerance from 1e-6 -> 1e-3) and ran unit bench: regained ~6% throughput but p99 still worse. posted run: 
```
rope_scale=1.2; relaxed_tol=1e-3 -> throughput +6% (was -13% -> now -7%)
```
maria: interesting. devon mentioned memcopies — maybe combined effect: occasional fallback increases fragmentation which then triggers more copies. can we avoid fallback unless contiguous KV layout is required?
devon: proposed guard: only disallow packed kernel when (num_kv_heads % head_block != 0) OR (rope_phase_variance > thresh). also add a bank_threshold so we avoid reshuffling banks on small deviations.
aj: sounds reasonable. any quick canary results?
sam: ran canary with num_kv_heads alignment check + bank_threshold=0.8. results: throughput -1.5% (almost neutral), p99 improved vs previous - 40% improvement from worst-case.
benchbot: scheduled canary rollout: canary/us-west2-dev -> 6 hosts, 24h ramp, fallback metric = rope_fallback_rate.
maria: I'll open a PR with: (1) head-alignment guard, (2) relaxed rope tolerance behind flag, (3) bank_threshold param exposed to runtime config.
lina: add regression test in perf harness: pump varied rope_scale values (0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2) and assert throughput drop <5% across bank_threshold sweep.
maria: yep will add. tagging @eng-ml and @eng-sre for visibility. any objections? :thinking_face:
aj: no objections. thanks for quick turn.
devon: follow-up: we should log selected_kernel + eligibility bitmap in traces so we can correlate fallbacks with sequences. small change but will help root cause.
maria: added to TODO in PR. will post PR number once ready.
